questions.q: What does Maxwell suggest reviewing before you start each day?
a: Your calendar, to spot the biggest learning opportunities
Your inbox, to clear the most urgent messages
Your goals, to rank them by importance
Your bank balance, to plan your spending
questions.why: Lesson one says to scan the day's appointments and prepare for the ones that offer the most to learn.

questions.q: What is the simplest way to practice creative thinking, according to the book?
a: Add one more option whenever you make a decision
Set aside an hour each day to brainstorm
Study the habits of creative geniuses
Keep a journal of your best ideas
questions.why: Lesson two argues that even one extra choice is a creative act, like wondering about a different cereal.

questions.q: Why did Alfred Nobel change his will after reading a newspaper?
a: It printed his obituary and he disliked how he would be remembered
It revealed that his brother had stolen his fortune
It praised a rival inventor above him
It reported that his factory was closing
questions.why: A reporter confused Nobel with his brother and described the dynamite inventor's death, prompting him to fund the prizes.

questions.q: What does the summary writer caution about the book's eleven thinking styles?
a: Use them as inspiration, not as a checklist
Practice all eleven every single morning
Ignore them and trust your instincts
Rank them before choosing a career
questions.why: The review says the list should not be treated as a set of habits, but as a source of inspiration for thinking itself.

questions.q: Which claim by Maxwell does the summary writer find hard to accept?
a: That all successful people think the same way
That thinking can be practiced daily
That big-picture thinking reduces stress
That unselfish thinking improves sleep
questions.why: The writer notes you can find successful people with opposite habits, so the idea that they all think alike is too simple.
